short: An armed uprising by Arab nationalists, supported by the British, successfully crippled Ottoman control over the Middle East.
full:
On 10 June 1916, Sharif Hussein bin Ali, the Emir of Mecca, initiated a rebellion against the Ottoman Empire in the Hejaz region. Supported by British military intelligence, notably T. E. Lawrence, the Arab forces employed asymmetric guerrilla warfare against Ottoman infrastructure. They systematically destroyed sections of the Hejaz Railway, isolating Ottoman garrisons and tying down thousands of troops who were forced to defend their supply lines.

The revolt expanded northward alongside the British offensive in Palestine, culminating in the capture of Damascus in October 1918. The campaign fatally undermined Ottoman authority in the Middle East and paved the way for the postwar partition of the region, although British and French secret agreements ultimately frustrated Arab aspirations for a unified, independent state.
